summary: Adds a regression test for the settled submitted-charge path in passportTrialCanReconsider. The test first asserts the positive baseline where the retained intent requestId matches the settled charge id, then mutates requestId and asserts both passportTrialCanReconsider and passportTrialCandidateBinding deny. The reported charge (attempt 9, purpose retry, settledAt non-null, head equal to target.base) satisfies all earlier guards, so the denial is decided solely by the requestId binding check at src/repair/passport-work-trial.ts:72; removing that guard makes the assertions fail. No production code changed and no defects found.

evidence: New test `Passport trial: a settled submitted charge must match the retained intent requestId` at tests/host/..._test.ts:176-191 uses a settled `submitted` charge, i.e. a case that passes without the requestId guard.

The same test first asserts canReconsider(record, charges) === true with the matching requestId (CHARGE) and then sets intent.requestId to `f`.repeat(64) and asserts denial plus passportTrialCandidateBinding(unbound, charges) === null.

src/repair/passport-work-trial.ts:72 (`intent.requestId !== charge.id`) is the only remaining guard for this fixture: attempt 9 equals counters.attempts, purpose `retry` matches, settledAt is set, and charge.head === target.base returns true just before binding checks.
